items.title: DeFranco Buddy — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Willy D. Simone was his name and he taught me for quite a few years.

ctx.x: Willy D. Simone was his name and he taught me for quite a few years. For about a year and a half for nothing, didn’t take any money. As years went on I began to play jobs and make a few dollars, sometimes three or four, five dollars a job. And Willy said, “Ok, you’re working now you have a dollar a lesson.” So I paid him a dollar a lesson. But he really set me in the right direction for being a clarinetist because he insisted on me being a well-schooled musician, and a well-schooled clarinetist. And he was by…
And was he, what kind of repertoire was he having you practice?
